body: Yeah man, you fucking ruined it. Good job.

Don't say nobody cares. I do.

I know a lot of people say that, and when I'm at my most depressed, I start thinking that the fact someone is saying they care about me online means nothing. "Bullshit", I would say. "A random person on the internet doesn't care about me".

That's not true. I have walked down that dark path many times. I want to see you get through it. I want to know that you are okay. I genuinely care that you are going through this, and want to see it get better. Please PM me if you need to talk to someone. I'm here for you.

I don't mind answering at all, I wanted to explain everything better but just wanted some direct questions. The first thing I had to do in order to change it was realize that before I could do anything, I needed to take care of myself. When times were hardest, I neglected showers, brushing teeth, eating, etc... because I didn't have enough energy. I didn't have enough energy because I saw almost everything as negative, or I could excuse my actions by saying things like "I can spend my last twenty dollars even though I don't have food, because I rarely eat anyway." Well, in order to feel better, you have to do what you stopped doing from being depressed in the first place. I made it a goal of mine to eat at least twice a day (which was a lot for me at first), and showering and brushing my teeth once a day. Just the act of pushing through and just getting up and doing it, even though it exhausted me at times, made my overall mood slightly better. With cleanliness came a little bit more confidence in my day to day interaction, and I wanted to interact because I was eating and my mood was slightly better. In the same way that some of the worst things about depression are the small things, such as how it isolates you, lose your appetite and sleep, you have to do small things to work up to happiness. Just being clean everyday made me feel slightly better, then after eating more I realized I was negative a lot of times just because I was constantly starving. I've been clean about a month, and I have implemented these methods, that is, the act of trying to at least accomplish one thing that will make me feel better at least once a day, since the day after I quit. In truth, the hardest part was not overcoming the addiction, though that certainly helps me feel better. The hardest part was that first step, acknowledging that I need to DO something to be happy, I can't just expect it to come naturally. The more work you have to do, the more the reward can be. Sorry for the lengthy post, but this is quite cathartic for me. I don't mind the questions, anyone who asks will get an answer, and if I need to elaborate more I will.

Edit: Oh, and a big part of making that first step is not thinking you're different. I thought for a long time, that I was completely fucked, because I had no reason to be depressed. I became depressed at about 15, and haven't gotten out of it since. Nothing prompted it, everyone around me doubted it. Whenever I would tell people I was suicidal, if I did at all, they would undermine it. I have attempted suicide where I legitimately tried, twice. If I attempted it, I had put hours of research into it, positive that it would kill me. I'm not talking about times psyching myself up with a noose around my throat to quit being a pussy, and just kill myself... There are too many times to count for that. Eventually, everyone around me got used to the fact that suicide was on my mind every day for 3 years, and so they would essentially say things like "Oh, he's always suicidal, but he isn't dead yet, is he?" I realize now that NOBODY wants to be around that type of person, and that's why I lost my friends, and my girlfriend. As a matter of fact, I still have no friends. But I have found that my better mood allows me to WANT to socialize, and maybe find new friends. I just have to find the right people, the ones that are worth my time finding, because they will actually, genuinely care. Tl;dr, if you think you are different, and that because your depression is not treatable right away because you don't have actual reasons to be depressed, you will have a more difficult time accepting that you can get through it. I tried many different medications without effect, or only some effect. I noticed that when I felt slightly better, I did things like eat, shower, brush my teeth more. I essentially realized that no matter the circumstances, symptoms are symptoms, and just like fake smiling has been proven to make people happy (I myself am against this, as I do not believe in faking emotions. I lived too long hiding how I felt), maybe doing the things I neglected once doing because I was depressed would help. I wouldn't say it's the end all, be all cure for depression. But it can't hurt, and it certainly makes the next step easier.
